hints: Use $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ with displacement $s = 0$ upon return to the ground.
Set $12t - 5t^2 = 0$ and solve for the non-zero time $t$.
walkthrough:
Apply the displacement equation for vertical motion under gravity when returning to ground ($s = 0$):
$$s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 \implies 0 = 12t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 12t - 5t^2$$

Factorize and solve for non-zero time $t$:
$$t(12 - 5t) = 0 \implies t = \frac{12}{5} = 2.4\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Vertical Motion: Uses $12t - \frac12gt^2 = 0$, obtaining The time is 2.4 s.

teacher_walkthrough: Particle P is projected vertically upwards with initial speed $u = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ under gravitational acceleration $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

When particle P returns to the ground, its vertical displacement from the starting point is zero ($s = 0$):
$$s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$$
$$0 = 12t - 5t^2$$
$$t(12 - 5t) = 0$$

Since $t > 0$ for the return time:
$$12 - 5t = 0 \implies t = \frac{12}{5} = 2.4\text{ s}$$

hints: Find when particle P reaches its highest point: $v_P = 12 - 10t = 0 \implies t = 1.2\text{ s}$.
Find when particle Q reaches its highest point: projected at $t = 1\text{ s}$ with speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $v_Q = 10 - 10(t - 1) = 0 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$.
Determine the intervals where both particles move upwards together ($1 < t < 1.2$) and downwards together ($2 < t < 2.4$).
walkthrough: Determine the critical times for both particles when velocities reverse direction:
Particle P: $v_P = 12 - 10t = 0 \implies t = 1.2\text{ s}$ (moves upwards for $0 < t < 1.2$, downwards for $1.2 < t < 2.4$).
Particle Q: starts at $t = 1\text{ s}$ with $u = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, reaches peak at $v_Q = 10 - 10(t - 1) = 0 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$ (moves upwards for $1 < t < 2$, downwards for $2 < t < 3$).

Identify the intervals of motion in the same direction:
$$\text{Both moving upwards: } 1 < t < 1.2$$
$$\text{Both moving downwards: } 2 < t < 2.4$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Vertical Motion: Uses both moving in the same direction for $1 < t < 1.2$.

teacher_walkthrough: To determine when the two particles move in the same direction, analyze the sign of velocity for each particle over time:

1. Particle P is projected at $t = 0$ with $u = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Its velocity is $v_P(t) = 12 - 10t$:
- Moves upwards ($v_P > 0$) for $0 < t < 1.2\text{ s}$.
- At rest at its peak at $t = 1.2\text{ s}$.
- Moves downwards ($v_P < 0$) for $1.2 < t < 2.4\text{ s}$.
- Hits ground at $t = 2.4\text{ s}$.

2. Particle Q is projected at $t = 1\text{ s}$ with $u = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Its velocity is $v_Q(t) = 10 - 10(t - 1) = 20 - 10t$:
- Moves upwards ($v_Q > 0$) for $1 < t < 2\text{ s}$.
- At rest at its peak at $t = 2\text{ s}$.
- Moves downwards ($v_Q < 0$) for $2 < t < 3\text{ s}$.
Now compare their directions of motion while both particles are in the air ($1 < t < 2.4$):
- For $1 < t < 1.2$: Both particles have positive velocity, so both are moving upwards.
- For $1.2 < t < 2$: P has negative velocity (moving down) while Q has positive velocity (moving up). Opposite directions.
- For $2 < t < 2.4$: Both particles have negative velocity, so both are moving downwards.

State the final set of values of $t$:
$$1 < t < 1.2 \quad \text{or} \quad 2 < t < 2.4$$
